basic_information.short_title: Power of Appointment in the Bangsamoro
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT DEFINING THE POWER OF APPOINTMENT IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker
Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Settles who in the Bangsamoro Government has the power to hire — the Chief Minister for senior posts, the Speaker for Parliament's own staff, and each head of office for everyone at Salary Grade 24 and below.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: A new government inherited ministries, bureaus, boards and commissions without a single rule on who could appoint whom. The act draws the line by salary grade, and requires appointments to be merit-based with attention to gender and ethnic balance.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Appointment authority is fixed by position rather than negotiated office by office. Salary Grade 25 and above sits with the Chief Minister; SG 24 and below sits with each head of office; Parliament's own staff sit with the Speaker.
who_will_be_affected: Anyone applying for a job in the Bangsamoro Government — which office decides your appointment now depends on the salary grade
Heads of ministries, offices, commissions, boards and agencies, whose appointing power is defined and limited
Heads of offices attached to a ministry, who do not hold this appointing power unless their own charter gives it
Staff of individual Members of Parliament, who are appointed only on that member's recommendation
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2020 — 15 days after publication in a newspaper of general circulation.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. Who hires you in the Bangsamoro Government depends on your salary grade: SG 25 and above is the Chief Minister, SG 24 and below is your head of office, and Parliament's own staff answer to the Speaker.
in_practice: Chief Minister: heads of ministries, offices, commissions, boards, agencies and bureaus; heads of Bangsamoro-owned or controlled corporations with original charters; deputy ministers and directors; and every position at Salary Grade 25 and above
Speaker: all career positions in Parliament, including coterminous and contractual posts and contracts of service — but must consult the Chief Minister for SG 25 and above
Heads of office: positions at Salary Grade 24 and below in their own agency
Staff of an individual MP: appointed only on that member's recommendation, and supervised by them directly
All appointments must be merit-based and consider gender and ethnic balance

for_specific_groups.Job applicants: The salary grade of the post tells you which office decides. SG 24 and below is decided inside the agency; SG 25 and above goes to the Chief Minister.
for_specific_groups.Heads of attached offices: Section 3 is explicit — if your office is attached to a ministry, you do not hold this appointing power unless the law creating your office says so.
for_specific_groups.Parliament staff: The Speaker appoints and administratively supervises, except for staff of individual members.
for_specific_groups.Women and non-Moro applicants: Section 5 requires gender and ethnic balance to be considered, though it sets no target or quota.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The whole Bangsamoro Government, its bureaus, boards, commissions, agencies, and Bangsamoro-owned or controlled corporations with original charters.
what_you_can_do: Check the salary grade of a post to know which office decides the appointment
If you work for an office attached to a ministry, check your own charter before assuming your head can appoint
watch_out_for: 'Strictly merit-based' and 'gender and ethnic balance' are stated as policy in Section 5, with no mechanism, target or remedy attached.
The act creates no appeals route for a rejected applicant and no penalty for an appointment made outside these rules.
It concentrates every senior appointment — SG 25 and up, across the whole government — in one office.

key_terms_explained.Salary Grade: The pay level of a government post. It is the dividing line this act uses: 24 and below, versus 25 and above.
key_terms_explained.Coterminous position: A post that ends when the official who appointed you leaves.
key_terms_explained.Original charter: A government corporation created by its own law rather than registered like a private company.
key_terms_explained.Attached office: An office placed under a ministry for policy and programme coordination while keeping some independence.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed 25 June 2020, approved by the Chief Minister on 29 June 2020.

benefits.headline: One clear rule on who appoints whom, drawn at Salary Grade 25.

direct_benefits.benefit: A published, checkable answer to 'who decides this appointment'
MPs choose and supervise their own office staff
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Members of Parliament and their staff

indirect_benefits: A stated merit standard for all Bangsamoro Government hiring
Gender and ethnic balance written into appointment policy
limitations: No quota, target or measurement for gender and ethnic balance.

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on the public — it governs government.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts for the public. Its one restriction falls on government: a head of an attached office may not exercise this appointing power unless its own charter provides otherwise.

penalties.note: The act sets no penalty for an appointment made outside these rules.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The appointing office named in Section 4 for that salary grade
where_to_complain.oversight: Civil Service rules apply to appointments under this act
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints or appeals procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: Nur applies for an SG 18 post at a Bangsamoro agency. The head of that office appoints — it does not go to the Chief Minister.
A director post at SG 26 opens. That is the Chief Minister's appointment, whatever the agency prefers.
An MP wants to hire a legislative aide. The Speaker makes the appointment, but only on that member's recommendation, and the member supervises the staffer directly.
An office attached to a ministry wants to hire its own staff. Unless the law that created it says so, it does not hold the appointing power this act describes.

key_provisions: Section 2 — Purpose: effective and efficient selection and appointment of officials and personnel across ministries, offices, bureaus, boards, commissions and agencies, based on merit and with due consideration to gender and ethnic balance.

Section 3 — Defines the power of appointment as the authority exercised under the Organic Law (RA 11054), regional laws, and Civil Service laws and rules. Defines heads of office, and provides that heads of offices attached to a ministry shall not exercise this appointing power unless the law creating the office provides otherwise.

Section 4(a)–(b) — The Chief Minister appoints heads of ministries, offices, commissions, boards, agencies and bureaus, and heads of Bangsamoro-owned or controlled corporations or entities with original charters; and likewise deputy ministers, directors or their equivalents, and all positions at Salary Grade 25 and above, unless a law expressly provides otherwise.

Section 4(c) — The Speaker exercises administrative supervision over Parliament's legislative personnel, staff and secretariat, and appoints to all career positions in Parliament including coterminous and contractual positions and contracts of service — consulting the Chief Minister on posts at Salary Grade 25 and above. Personnel under the office of an individual Member of Parliament are appointed only on that member's recommendation, and that member exercises direct supervision and control over them.
Section 4(d) — Heads of offices appoint officials and employees at Salary Grade 24 and below in their own agencies.

Section 5 — Appointments are to be made through an independent, strictly merit-based and credible placement and hiring process across all offices, agencies and institutions, and shall consider gender and ethnic balance.
Section 8 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of general circulation.

related_legislation.related_note: Grounded on Article VII, Section 32 of the Organic Law (RA 11054). Sits alongside the Bangsamoro Civil Service Code (BAA 17), which governs the wider terms of public employment in the region.

citizen_questions.q: Who decides whether I get the job?
citizen_questions.a: It depends on the salary grade. Salary Grade 24 and below is appointed by the head of the office you applied to. Salary Grade 25 and above is appointed by the Chief Minister.

The Speaker, who also administratively supervises them — but must consult the Chief Minister for posts at Salary Grade 25 and above. Staff of an individual MP are appointed only on that member's recommendation.

citizen_questions.q: Does my head of office always have the power to hire?
citizen_questions.a: Not if the office is attached to a ministry. Section 3 says heads of attached offices do not exercise this appointing power unless the law creating the office provides otherwise.

citizen_questions.q: Does the law require fair hiring?
citizen_questions.a: It requires an independent, strictly merit-based and credible process, and says appointments shall consider gender and ethnic balance. It sets no target and provides no remedy if that is ignored.

citizen_questions.q: Can I appeal if I am passed over?
citizen_questions.a: Not under this act — it creates no appeals procedure. Civil Service laws and rules still apply to appointments made under it.

display_header.what_this_does: Fixes who appoints whom across the Bangsamoro Government, drawn at Salary Grade 25.
display_header.who_it_affects: Government job applicants · agency heads · Parliament staff

views.simple: Sets who has the power to hire in the Bangsamoro Government: the Chief Minister from Salary Grade 25 up, heads of office at 24 and below, and the Speaker for Parliament's own staff.
